name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description:
Information Systems - academic year 23/24
Course Project
Scenario

La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of materials and products for the home. To improve the efficiency of its operations and the service to customers, the company is re-designing its information system. The details follow.

La Reine Marlene has a wide network of suppliers. The suppliers of La Reine Marlene will have to register in the system, providing their credentials and company details, including VAT number, address and the IBAN for payments. Registered suppliers can make proposals of their own products by entering in the system the following information for each product: category, sale price (the one that La Reine Marlene must pay to the supplier), availability, photo, description, guaranteed delivery time. The product categories are 16: Garden, Bathroom, Air Conditioning, Lighting, Decoration, Flooring, Doors and Windows, Carpentry, Kitchen, Storage, Tools, Electricity, Construction, Paints, Hardware, Furniture. Once a proposal has been entered, the supplier can no longer modify it until they receive a response notification.

When a supplier enters a proposal, the administration department of La Reine Marlene receives a message notifying the presence of a new proposal from the suppliers. At that point, it must verify the proposal and select one of the following options: Order accepted, Revisions requested, Order rejected. If the order is accepted, a separate order management process will start, to which the information on the price to be displayed in the store is added, so that this information will already be available in the subsequent processes. If instead revisions have been requested, they must be made explicit in a comment: at that point the supplier receives a notification and has 5 working days to modify the proposal, entering reply comments, and re-submit it. If the proposal has been modified within the 5 working days, then the proposal evaluation process restarts, otherwise the proposal is deleted from the system and the supplier notified. The administrators receive a reminder every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal that is waiting to be validated. A proposal that has not been verified within 10 working days is automatically rejected, and a specific message is sent to the supplier.

Once the products ordered from the suppliers are shipped and arrive at the destination La Reine Marlene site (there are dozens of them throughout Italy), they are entered in the inventory of all the products available in the store (La Reine Marlene has no warehouse: any available product is on display). Each product is catalogued according to its category, available quantity and location in the store. The location in the store is entered directly by the goods receiving staff: when an order is delivered, the staff members must verify each product. If there are no problems, the operator confirms the product and the system proposes a list of possible placements: the location is chosen, and the product is physically handed over to whoever will take care of its placement in the store and of printing the price to be displayed. Should there be problems with any product, the operator reports it by entering a comment and the product does not enter the store. At the end of these operations of verification of an order arrival, the operator closes the procedure and a new process starts, managed by the order department: if all the products have been accepted, the order is concluded and the payment sent. Otherwise, the order is updated and a new arrival that completes it is awaited. In both cases specific messages are sent to the supplier.

The system keeps track of stock in real time. An automatic notification is sent to the order department when a product reaches a critical reorder level (where it is specified). The administrators, in fact, can schedule automatic reordering and replenishment actions for specific products, in order to maintain an optimal inventory. In case of automatic reordering, a message is sent to the pre-established supplier, who has two working days to confirm acceptance of the order. In the absence of critical thresholds and of the related automation, the new order is managed by the order department with a separate process.

Customers looking for materials for the home can purchase the products both through the physical store and through the online store. In the online store, customers who have registered on the site can browse the digital catalogue, specify the desired products and quantities and complete the order. The system automatically calculates the order total, including taxes and shipping costs. Customers can choose among different payment options: credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, the La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer with the affiliated banks. Once the order is paid, the system keeps track of deliveries in real time. Customers receive a link by email through which they can follow the status of their shipments. In addition, those who have given consent to the use of the mobile phone number will receive notifications on updates to delivery times. Once the product arrives at its destination, the order is tracked as concluded. Deliveries are managed by partner companies, and each online purchase is randomly assigned to a shipping carrier. Consider that the online store is also accessible through a dedicated app: the operations and procedures are the same as those of the site.

La Reine Marlene offers a complete customer service through the information system. Customers can ask questions, request assistance or make complaints directly through the system. Support tickets are automatically assigned to a customer service agent. Every time a ticket is assigned, the agent receives a notification and has 24 hours to respond (if this does not happen, the ticket is reassigned to a new operator, and the statistics updated). The customer is informed upon receipt of the reply message, and has five working days to respond: otherwise, the ticket is considered closed.

Finally, the system collects data on orders, sales, inventory, customer support. These data are used to analyze performance and make strategic decisions.
highLevelGoals: Suppliers aim to easily register, propose products with all necessary details, and respond to revision requests to get their products accepted by La Reine Marlene.
Suppliers need to be informed promptly about the status of their product proposals (accepted, rejected, revisions requested) and receive automatic reorder requests.
The Administration Department Staff aims to efficiently review supplier proposals, make timely decisions (accept, reject, request revisions), and ensure proper follow-up on revised proposals.
The Administration Department Staff seeks to schedule and manage automatic reordering and replenishment actions to prevent stockouts and maintain an optimal product inventory.
Goods Receiving Staff aims to efficiently verify delivered products against orders, identify and report any issues, and correctly assign products to their store locations.
Goods Receiving Staff needs to ensure that products are correctly catalogued, their quantities updated in the inventory, and their physical location in the store is accurately recorded.
Order Department Staff aims to ensure that all accepted products from an order are accounted for, payments are processed correctly, and orders are concluded or updated as necessary.
Order Department Staff seeks to be notified when products reach critical reorder levels and to initiate new orders to maintain sufficient stock.
Customers aim to easily find desired products, add them to their cart, and complete purchases through various payment options, both online and in physical stores.
Customers need to be able to track the status of their orders and deliveries in real-time and receive notifications about delivery updates.
Customers aim to easily submit questions, requests for assistance, or complaints and receive timely and helpful responses from customer service agents.
Customer Service Agents aim to receive notifications for new support tickets and respond to customer inquiries, assistance requests, and complaints within established timeframes.
Customer Service Agents need to manage their assigned tickets, provide clear responses, and ensure tickets are resolved or escalated appropriately.
Managers/Executives aim to access and analyze comprehensive data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support to understand business performance.
Managers/Executives need to leverage system-collected data to identify trends, evaluate operational efficiency, and make informed strategic decisions for the company.
lowLevelGoals: The system should allow a supplier to create a new account by providing their company details and contact information.
The system should allow a supplier to submit a new product proposal, including product category, sale price, availability, photo, description, and guaranteed delivery time.
The system should allow a supplier to edit the details of a previously submitted product proposal.
The system should allow a supplier to view revision comments and resubmit a modified product proposal.
The system should allow a supplier to confirm acceptance of an automatic reorder request within two working days.
The system should send an automated notification to the supplier when their product proposal is accepted.
The system should send an automated notification to the supplier when their product proposal is rejected.
The system should send an automated notification to the supplier when revisions are requested for their product proposal.
The system should send an automated notification to the supplier when an automatic reorder for their product is initiated.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to view a list of all product proposals awaiting review.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to access and review the detailed information of a single product proposal.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to mark a product proposal as 'accepted'.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to mark a product proposal as 'rejected' and provide a reason.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to request revisions for a product proposal, providing specific feedback to the supplier.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to monitor the status of proposals that have been sent back for revisions.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to add the retail price to be displayed in the store for an accepted product proposal.
The system should automatically delete a product proposal if the supplier does not modify it within 5 working days of a revision request.
The system should automatically reject a product proposal if the Administration Department Staff does not verify it within 10 working days.
The system should send an automated reminder to Administration Department Staff every 48 hours about the presence of a proposal waiting to be validated.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to set up automatic reorder rules for accepted products, specifying thresholds and quantities.
The system should allow Administration Department Staff to adjust the parameters of existing automatic reorder schedules.
The system should provide Administration Department Staff with a list of products scheduled for automatic reordering.
The system should allow Goods Receiving Staff to scan or input delivered product details and compare them against the corresponding purchase order.
The system should allow Goods Receiving Staff to log and report any mismatches, damages, or missing items in a product delivery.
The system should allow Goods Receiving Staff to specify the physical store location where a delivered product will be placed.
The system should automatically create a new product entry in the inventory when a previously uncatalogued product is delivered and verified.
The system should automatically increment the stock quantity for products that have been successfully delivered and verified.
The system should store and display the precise physical location (e.g., aisle, shelf) of each product within the store.
The system should allow Order Department Staff to mark a purchase order as fully completed after all products are received and payments processed.
The system should allow Order Department Staff to record and confirm payment for a completed order.
The system should allow Order Department Staff to update an ongoing order to reflect partial deliveries and await completion of the remaining items.
The system should send an automated notification to Order Department Staff when a product's inventory level falls below its predefined critical threshold.
The system should allow Order Department Staff to create and submit a new purchase order for products needing replenishment.
The system should allow customers to filter and view products based on different categories.
The system should allow customers to search for products using keywords or product names.
The system should allow customers to add desired products to their virtual shopping cart.
The system should allow customers to initiate the purchase process for items in their shopping cart.

The system should offer customers various payment options including credit card (Visa or Mastercard), Paypal, Satispay, La Reine Marlene purchasing card, or immediate online bank transfer during checkout.
The system should process the payment and finalize an online order.
The system should allow point-of-sale (POS) terminals to process payments and finalize in-store orders.
The system should allow customers to view the current processing and shipping status of their placed orders via a tracking link sent by email.
The system should send automated SMS notifications to customers regarding changes in their delivery status (e.g., shipped, out for delivery, delivered) if they have consented.
The system should allow customers to submit questions or requests for assistance through a dedicated interface.
The system should allow customers to submit formal complaints regarding products or services.
The system should deliver responses from customer service agents to the customer's support inquiry or complaint.
The system should allow customers to reply to an existing support ticket within 5 working days.
The system should alert Customer Service Agents when a new customer support inquiry or complaint is submitted.
The system should allow Customer Service Agents to view a list of support tickets automatically assigned to them.
The system should allow Customer Service Agents to compose and send responses to customer questions or requests for assistance.
The system should allow Customer Service Agents to compose and send responses to customer complaints.
The system should automatically assign new support tickets to an available customer service agent.
The system should allow Customer Service Agents to change the status of a ticket (e.g., 'open', 'in progress', 'resolved', 'escalated').
The system should allow Customer Service Agents to escalate a ticket to a higher level of support or a different department.
The system should automatically reassign a support ticket to another agent if the current agent does not respond within 24 hours.
The system should allow Managers/Executives to generate reports detailing sales figures over specified periods.
The system should allow Managers/Executives to generate reports showing current stock levels and movement of products.
The system should allow Managers/Executives to generate reports on customer support performance, such as response times and resolution rates.
The system should provide Managers/Executives with a customizable dashboard displaying real-time KPIs related to sales, inventory, and customer service.
The system should provide tools for Managers/Executives to visualize and analyze sales data to identify patterns and trends.
The system should calculate and display inventory turnover rates to help Managers/Executives assess inventory efficiency.
